complexity.notes: Correct but does redundant work: maxDepth re-walks each subtree once per ancestor. A single ||bottom-up pass that returns each subtree's height (or a sentinel like -1 once an imbalance is found)|| would reach O(n) time with the same O(h) stack. Space is O(h) recursion depth — O(log n) for balanced trees, O(n) in the worst case of a fully skewed tree.
complexity.summary: Top-down recursion: at each node it checks the balance condition by recomputing the height of both subtrees with a separate maxDepth traversal, then recurses into the children. Since heights are recomputed at every level, a node at depth d pays for its subtree's height repeatedly, giving O(n log n) on balanced trees and O(n^2) on skewed ones.
